findings.title: Gaza aid delivery fleet reportedly near collapse amid spare-parts, tyre and engine-oil restrictions
findings.publisher: Al-Quds, reporting from Haaretz interviews and Gaza transport association statements
findings.affected_population_system: Aid logistics, truck drivers, humanitarian cargo distribution, and linked health-worker transport. Transport association representative says about 250 old trucks available versus 600–700 needed, with existing vehicles regularly breaking down and missing oil, tyres and spare parts.
findings.finding_summary: Al-Quds published a report at 15:26 Jerusalem time on 16 November, describing warnings that aging Gaza aid trucks may cease operating as replacement tyres, engine oil and parts are unavailable. Nahid Shuheibar, identified as head of Gaza's private transport association, says 250 trucks remain against an estimated 600–700 needed. UltraSawt separately cites first-hand Haaretz reporting and the same interview, including a response from Israeli coordination authorities characterizing the restricted items as dual-use. This is a newly reported, attributable operational-capacity estimate and risk, NOT confirmation that all truck deliveries have stopped or that a new closure occurred during the observation window.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: أوضح ناهض شحيبر، رئيس جمعية النقل الخاص في غزة أن زيادة كميات المساعدات عند المعابر لن تحل الأزمة ما لم يتم إصلاح الشاحنات المتهالكة.

bounded_discovery_context.new_information: Current estimated usable truck fleet approximately 250 versus estimated 600–700 needed, with shortages of imported replacement parts, tyres and engine oil.
bounded_discovery_context.assessment: Not a confirmed completed collapse; an attributed logistics-capacity warning in new reporting. Previous heartbeat did not contain this dated transport-capacity estimate.
bounded_discovery_context.source_caveat: Al-Quds and UltraSawt summarize the same original Haaretz interviews and should not be counted as independent primary corroboration.
